title: daemon_status
description:
Robot -> client. Motion-stack health, as observed by the BRIDGE rather than reported by the daemon -- the daemon cannot tell you it is down. This is why the message is session-layer and has no daemon-layer counterpart.

Distinct from transport health: the peer connection can be perfect while this reads offline, and in that state the robot DROPS every control frame. A client that jogs without checking this will see a robot that ignores it with no error anywhere.

While offline the bridge rebroadcasts every few seconds (the channel is unreliable and there is no telemetry to imply liveness). Clients SHOULD de-duplicate on the whole triple state+reason+detail before surfacing it, so the repeats do not spam a UI or a log.

state.description: A frame with a missing or empty state MUST be dropped and the previous health kept -- never coerced to offline, which would invent an outage.

reason.description: Machine-readable cause when offline. Open set -- treat an unknown value as 'offline for a reason this client does not model', never as an error. L3 sends "unauthorized" (motion authority refused) or "unreachable" (motion disabled or daemon down). The L2 bridge sends "connection_lost" when the daemon closes the socket -- the most common value in practice -- or forwards the daemon's own fatal error code, e.g. "startup_positions", "bus_lost", "version_mismatch".

detail.description: Human-readable elaboration. For operators and logs; never parse it.

robot_local_mic_muted.description: Robot-side local mute. Robots boot muted and someone at the robot unmutes; this rides here rather than on telemetry because telemetry only flows while the daemon is UP, and a boot-muted robot with a down daemon would otherwise render an unmuted-looking call UI.
